_comment: The registry of traditional songs. One entry per page. Adding a song means adding a row here and nothing else in code: the scaffold fetches its `ref`, the builder names the file from `n` and `slug`, and songs-index.mjs writes its card into the home page under `category`.
_comment_selection: Only songs whose Hebrew has a citable source are here, because the pipeline refuses to let an author type Hebrew. That rules out the folk repertoire whose words exist on lyric sites and nowhere citable (Hevenu Shalom Aleichem, Siman Tov, Zum Gali Gali), and it rules out post-1928 melodies whose text is not the point (Erev Shel Shoshanim, Bashana Haba'a).
_comment_dedup: Nothing here duplicates a page the site already ships. Hine Ma Tov, Esa Einai and Shir HaMa'alot are absent because Psalms 133, 121 and 126 already have singable pages with their own grid and tempo; Adon Olam, Shalom Aleichem, Eshet Chayil, Eliyahu HaNavi and Yevarechecha are absent because prayers-012, songs-003, shabbat-005, shabbat-013 and shabbat-006 already carry them.

songs._was: Ki Eshmera Shabbat (Abraham ibn Ezra) held this slot and was dropped, not because of the song but because of the sources: Sefaria carries it only in Daat Siddur Ashkenaz, entirely unpointed, and there is no vocalized edition of it anywhere in the library. A site that teaches reading cannot ship 22 lines of bare consonants, and the scaffold now refuses them rather than pretending. Shabbos Hayom is the same slot in the meal, from the Metsudah edition, fully pointed.
